records.name: Church random sequence (Church's 1940 effective selection formulation)
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence with limiting digit frequency p
records.effective_resources: effectively calculable selection rule whose choice at each stage depends on previously seen terms, in Church's formulation
records.measure_assumptions: frequency formulation rather than an explicit measure-test definition
records.relativization: not treated in inspected source
records.formal_summary: A sequence is admitted as random only if its limiting frequency is p and every infinite subsequence selected by an effectively calculable admissible rule retains limiting frequency p.
cautions: Later literature uses related terms such as Church stochasticity; P1-S001 does not assert identity across all conventions without a dedicated terminology check.

records.name: Martin-Löf randomness on fair-coin Cantor space
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence X in 2^ω
records.effective_resources: uniformly computably enumerable sequence of effectively open sets
records.measure_assumptions: uniform/fair-coin measure; test levels have measure at most 2^-n
records.relativization: Standalone oracle-relative Martin-Löf randomness is DEF-0019; n-randomness as jump-relativized Martin-Löf randomness is DEF-0020.
records.formal_summary: A Martin-Löf test is a uniformly c.e. sequence of effectively open sets with μ(U_n) ≤ 2^-n. X is Martin-Löf random iff it is not in the intersection of any Martin-Löf test (equivalently, it passes every such test).
cautions: P1-S007 object guard: SRC-0047 explicitly applies these Martin-Löf tests to infinite binary sequences and distinguishes them from tests applied to finite strings.

P1-S011 historical guard: SRC-0001's original fair-coin syntax uses r.e. nested, extension-closed sequential critical regions and finite critical level under a universal test; DEF-0002 is the modern uniformly effectively open normal form, not a verbatim quotation of the 1966 syntax.
SRC-0001 Section IV separately handles arbitrary computable sequential distributions. Do not use that historical extension to overwrite the modern generalized-measure records DEF-0005 or DEF-0033.

records.name: Schnorr randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real in fair-coin Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: uniformly c.e. open test levels with an effectively controlled measure: in SRC-0008, μ(U_n)≤2^-n and n↦μ(U_n) is computable; SRC-0024/SRC-0028 use the equivalent exact-measure normalization μ(U_n)=2^-n
records.framework: effective null tests with computable level measures; equivalent bounded-rate computable-martingale and total-Solovay formulations are separately indexed
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space in the inspected primary formulations
records.relativization: Ordinary oracle-relative Schnorr randomness is DEF-0022. Uniformly relative Schnorr randomness is the distinct weaker convention DEF-0024 used in SRC-0032's van-Lambalgen theorem.
records.formal_summary: A sequence is Schnorr random iff it passes every uniformly effective open test whose level measures are themselves computable. The 2002 primary formulation uses μ(U_n)≤2^-n with computable n↦μ(U_n); later primary sources inspected here use an exact μ(U_n)=2^-n normal form.

source_support.pointer: preprint p. 4; retained P1-S001 survey provenance

cautions: P1-S001 provenance is preserved. P1-S002 corrects a convention ambiguity: computable level measures are the substantive Schnorr restriction; μ(U_n)=2^-n is an inspected normal-form convention, not the only baseline statement.
The original 1971 Schnorr book/article are catalogued as SRC-0022/SRC-0023 at METADATA_ONLY; their internal statements were not silently substituted.
P1-S003 distinguishes ordinary oracle relativization from uniformly relative/truth-table Schnorr randomness; they must not be silently identified.

records.name: Computable randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / subset A of N identified with its characteristic sequence
records.effective_resources: total computable (historically: recursive) martingales; rational-valued martingales suffice in the inspected primary formulations
records.framework: betting / martingale; equivalent computably graded effective tests are indexed separately
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin Cantor-space/fair-betting martingale equation M(σ)=(M(σ0)+M(σ1))/2
records.relativization: Ordinary oracle-relative computable randomness is DEF-0021. Uniformly relative computable randomness is DEF-0025; SRC-0032 gives a source-supported separation showing the uniform-relative notion can be weaker.
records.formal_summary: A sequence X is computably random iff no computable martingale has unbounded capital along X, i.e. no computable martingale M has limsup_n M(X↾n)=∞.

source_support.pointer: preprint p. 4; retained P1-S001 survey provenance

cautions: 'Recursive randomness' is recorded as a historical/source term for this computable-martingale notion, not as a blanket alias for every historical use of 'recursive random'.
P1-S003 distinguishes ordinary A-computable-martingale relativization from uniform-family relativization.

records.name: Martin-Löf test for a computable measure on Cantor space
records.object_domain: Cantor space 2^ω equipped with computable probability measure μ
records.effective_resources: uniformly effectively open/c.e. test components; equivalently average-bounded lower-semicomputable integral tests in inspected primary sources
records.measure_assumptions: P is a computable Borel probability measure on Cantor space; cylinder values are uniformly computable; P(U_n)≤2^-n
records.relativization: uniform-in-measure version is DEF-0006
records.formal_summary: For a computable probability measure P on 2^ω, a Martin-Löf P-test is a uniformly effectively open sequence (U_n) with P(U_n)≤2^-n; a real is P-Martin-Löf random iff it avoids every resulting effective P-null set. SRC-0038 also gives the equivalent average-bounded lower-semicomputable integral-test form.
cautions: This record is Cantor-space specific. The general computable-probability-space notion is DEF-0033.
Computability of P is substantive here; DEF-0006 separately records uniform tests that take an arbitrary measure as a parameter.

records.name: Uniform randomness test with the probability measure as a parameter
records.object_domain: pair (P,x): in SRC-0038, x∈2^ω and P is an arbitrary Borel probability measure on Cantor space; SRC-0011 develops the corresponding uniform-test machinery on computable metric spaces
records.effective_resources: a nonnegative test function lower semicomputable jointly in the point and a representation/name of the measure; fixed-P tests may use P as an oracle/parameter in the source-specific representation
records.measure_assumptions: P need not be computable in the arbitrary-measure uniform framework; t satisfies ∫t(x,P)dP(x)≤1 for every P
records.relativization: uniformity is in the measure parameter, not ordinary oracle relativization of the point-randomness notions from P1-S003
records.formal_summary: A uniform test is jointly lower semicomputable in (x,P), nonnegative, and has P-integral at most 1 for every probability measure P. For a fixed P, restriction gives a P-test; conversely SRC-0038 Theorem 5.12 uniformizes a P-relative test at P up to a constant. SRC-0011 proves the analogous universal uniform-test machinery for computable metric spaces.
cautions: Do not identify 'uniform in the measure parameter' with Miyabe-Rute uniform oracle relativization from DEF-0024/DEF-0025.
The arbitrary-measure version permits noncomputable measures; fixed computable-measure Martin-Löf randomness is DEF-0005/DEF-0033 depending on the ambient space.

records.name: Kolmogorov–Loveland randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence
records.effective_resources: computable non-monotonic betting strategies that may choose which bit to bet on next
records.measure_assumptions: binary fair-betting setting of inspected source abstract
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S001
records.formal_summary: X is KL-random iff no computable non-monotonic betting strategy succeeds on X with unbounded gain while successively betting on bits of X.
cautions: The coincidence question with Martin-Löf randomness is QST-0001, not an established equivalence.

records.name: Low for Martin-Löf randomness
records.object_domain: oracle/set A
records.effective_resources: comparison of unrelativized and A-relative Martin-Löf randomness
records.measure_assumptions: standard fair-coin Martin-Löf randomness setting
records.relativization: Intrinsic ordinary oracle relativization: A is the oracle in DEF-0019. This is not the uniform-relative Schnorr/computable convention distinguished in P1-S003.
records.formal_summary: A is low for Martin-Löf randomness iff every unrelativized Martin-Löf-random real X remains Martin-Löf random relative to A; equivalently, in SRC-0009 notation, MLR^A = MLR.

source_support.pointer: preprint pp. 3-4, low-for-R paragraph and principal coincidence discussion

cautions: The quantification is over unrelativized Martin-Löf random reals: every such real must remain Martin-Löf random under ordinary oracle-A tests.

Low for Martin-Löf randomness is a definition distinct from K-triviality (DEF-0008), low for K (DEF-0063) and base for randomness (DEF-0009); equivalence is recorded only through inspected theorem records.
Do not substitute uniformly relative Schnorr/computable randomness for DEF-0019.

records.name: K-triviality
records.object_domain: set/real A
records.effective_resources: prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity K
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: not part of the definition recorded here
records.formal_summary: A is K-trivial iff there is a constant b such that for every n, K(A↾n) ≤ K(n)+b, where K is prefix-free/self-delimiting Kolmogorov complexity and K(n) is the prefix-free complexity of n under the source convention.
cautions: The inequality quantifies over all initial-segment lengths n with one additive constant independent of n.
K is prefix-free complexity; do not replace it by Martin-Löf 1966's conditional plain-complexity quantity or by an infinite-sequence randomness predicate.
K-triviality is not defined as lowness or baseness; the coincidence with DEF-0007, DEF-0063 and DEF-0009 is theorem-level.

records.name: Base for R-randomness
records.object_domain: set B relative to a specified randomness notion R
records.effective_resources: Turing reducibility plus relativized R-randomness
records.measure_assumptions: inherited from R
records.relativization: essential: Z is R-random relative to B
records.formal_summary: For a relativizable randomness notion R, B is a base for R-randomness iff there exists a real Z with B≤_T Z such that Z is R-random relative to B.

source_support.pointer: Definition 1.2, preprint p. 2; Theorem 2.1 and surrounding section for R = 1-randomness

cautions: Being a base is an existential property involving some Z above B in Turing reducibility; it is not the universal preservation condition defining low for randomness.
For 1-randomness, the inspected theorem package identifies bases with K-trivial sets (THM-0004); no analogous equivalence for an arbitrary R is inferred.

records.name: Plain Kolmogorov complexity C
records.object_domain: finite binary string σ
records.effective_resources: fixed optimal description machine in the plain-machine model
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: not treated in this record
records.formal_summary: C(σ) is the length of a shortest description/program for σ on a fixed optimal plain description machine, up to the usual additive-machine constant.

records.name: Prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity K
records.object_domain: finite binary string σ
records.effective_resources: fixed optimal prefix-free description machine
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: not treated in this record
records.formal_summary: K(σ) is the length of a shortest prefix-free description/program for σ on a fixed optimal prefix-free machine, up to an additive constant.

source_support.pointer: self-delimiting H framework and Theorem 4.2 in the article reprint

cautions: K(σ) is a complexity of a finite string. It becomes an infinite-sequence randomness characterization only through a quantified initial-segment condition such as THM-0001; finite-string incompressibility is not itself a standalone infinite-sequence randomness notion.

records.name: Kurtz randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real α in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: computably enumerable (Σ^0_1) measure-one open classes in the weak-1 formulation
records.framework: measure-one effective typicality test; equivalent weak-test/martingale formulations are source-supported in SRC-0029
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space; tested class has measure 1
records.relativization: Ordinary oracle-relative Kurtz randomness is DEF-0023 in the martingale/rate convention inspected in SRC-0031; weak-n oracle tests remain source-supported separately by SRC-0027.
records.formal_summary: α is Kurtz random iff α belongs to every computably enumerable (Σ^0_1) class of measure one; equivalently it avoids every effectively closed null class.

source_support.pointer: publisher abstract explicitly states the definition

cautions: Unqualified 'Kurtz randomness' / 'weak randomness' denotes the n=1 level here. Weak 2-randomness is strictly stronger and is not treated as an alias.
SRC-0025 is the original Kurtz thesis but remains METADATA_ONLY; exact definition support comes from inspected later primary sources.

records.name: Weak n-randomness
records.object_domain: real α in Cantor space 2^ω, with integer n≥1
records.effective_resources: Σ^0_n definability of measure-one classes
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure; α must belong to every Σ^0_n class of measure 1
records.relativization: SRC-0027 says relative weak-n randomness is obtained by adding an oracle to the tests. The comparison notion n-randomness is now normalized separately as DEF-0020: Martin-Löf randomness relative to ∅^(n−1).
records.formal_summary: For n≥1, α is weakly n-random iff it belongs to every Σ^0_n class of measure one.
cautions: The adjective 'weak' is indexed by n; it must not be collapsed into unqualified Kurtz/weak randomness without the level.
Do not infer equivalence between weak-n indexing and jump-relativized n-randomness: SRC-0027 states only the strict sandwich captured in THM-0017.

records.name: Weak 2-randomness
records.object_domain: real α in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: avoidance of Π^0_2 nullsets; equivalently computable nested c.e.-open tests whose measures converge to 0 without an effective rate
records.framework: Π^0_2 nullset avoidance / generalized Martin-Löf tests
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure; generalized-test level measures tend to zero
records.relativization: SRC-0027 states relative randomness is obtained by adding an oracle to the tests
records.formal_summary: α is weakly 2-random iff it avoids every Π^0_2 nullset; equivalently it passes every generalized Martin-Löf test. The key contrast with Martin-Löf tests is that μ(U_n)→0 need not have a computable convergence rate.
cautions: Weak 2-randomness is a higher Kurtz/weak-n level and is not synonymous with unqualified Kurtz randomness (weak 1-randomness).

records.name: Generalized Martin-Löf test (for weak 2-randomness)
records.object_domain: computable sequence (U_n) of c.e. open subsets of Cantor space
records.effective_resources: uniform c.e. openness and computable indexing; no required computable modulus for measure convergence
records.measure_assumptions: U_n⊇U_{n+1} and lim_n μ(U_n)=0
records.relativization: SRC-0027 states oracle-relative versions are obtained by adding an oracle to the tests
records.formal_summary: A generalized Martin-Löf test is a computable nested sequence of c.e. open sets U_n with μ(U_n)→0. Unlike an ML test it imposes no prescribed/effective speed of convergence.

source_support.pointer: Definition 2.2 and following sentence on speed of convergence

records.name: Total Solovay test (Schnorr form)
records.object_domain: computable sequence (V_i) of c.e. open subsets of Cantor space
records.effective_resources: uniformly effective enumeration plus computability of the finite total measure sum
records.measure_assumptions: Σ_i μ(V_i) is finite and is a computable real
records.relativization: not treated in the inspected source record
records.formal_summary: A total Solovay test is a computable collection of c.e. open sets whose sum of measures is finite and computable; a real passes if it belongs to only finitely many levels.

records.name: Computably graded test
records.object_domain: Martin-Löf test (V_n) on Cantor space equipped with a computable grading map f:2^{<ω}×ω→R
records.effective_resources: computable grading f controlling conditional/local level measure over cylinders and finite prefix-free refinements
records.framework: restricted effective null test equivalent to computable martingale betting
records.measure_assumptions: for each n, local bounds imply μ(V_n)≤2^-n; Definition 5 of SRC-0024 gives the three exact grading inequalities
records.relativization: not treated in the inspected source record
records.formal_summary: A Martin-Löf test is computably graded when a computable f supplies the local measure bounds and prefix-free additivity/subadditivity conditions of SRC-0024 Definition 5; passing all such tests characterizes computable randomness.

records.name: Martin-Löf randomness relative to an oracle A
records.object_domain: oracle A∈2^ω and real X∈2^ω
records.effective_resources: a uniformly A-c.e. sequence of string sets/open classes forming a Martin-Löf test
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space; each level has measure at most 2^-i in the inspected formulation
records.relativization: Intrinsic: c.e. enumeration/effectivity of the test is computed relative to oracle A.
records.formal_summary: An A-Martin-Löf test is a Martin-Löf test whose components are uniformly c.e. relative to A. X is Martin-Löf random relative to A (A-random) iff X passes every A-Martin-Löf test.

source_support.pointer: introductory A-Martin-Löf-test definition, printed around p. 4

cautions: The P1-S003 normalized record is only for fair-coin Cantor space; it is not silently generalized to arbitrary measures/spaces.
SRC-0032 notes that uniform-relative ML randomness coincides with ordinary relative ML randomness, unlike the Schnorr/computable situation.

records.name: n-randomness via oracle jumps
records.object_domain: real X∈2^ω and integer n≥1
records.effective_resources: Martin-Löf tests relative to the (n−1)-st Turing jump ∅^(n−1)
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space in the inspected sources
records.relativization: X is n-random exactly when X is Martin-Löf random relative to ∅^(n−1).
records.formal_summary: For n≥1, X is n-random iff X is Martin-Löf random relative to the oracle ∅^(n−1). Thus n=1 recovers ordinary Martin-Löf randomness.
cautions: This is the source-supported jump convention used to read THM-0017; weak n-randomness DEF-0014 is a different indexed hierarchy.

records.name: Computable randomness relative to an oracle A
records.object_domain: oracle A and infinite binary sequence B
records.effective_resources: martingales M whose real values M(σ) are uniformly computable using A as an oracle
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin martingale setting
records.relativization: Intrinsic: the martingale is A-computable.
records.formal_summary: B is computably random relative to A iff no A-computable martingale succeeds on B.

source_support.pointer: Definition 1.7 and immediately following relativization paragraph

cautions: Do not identify this ordinary oracle relativization with uniformly relative computable randomness DEF-0025; SRC-0032 Corollary 5.4 separates them.

records.name: Schnorr randomness relative to an oracle A (ordinary martingale relativization in SRC-0031)
records.object_domain: oracle A and infinite binary sequence R
records.effective_resources: A-recursive rate function r, A-recursive martingale mg and A-recursive bound function f in Property 1.1
records.measure_assumptions: binary fair-betting/Cantor-space setting of the inspected paper
records.relativization: Property 1.1 relativizes the rate, martingale and bound resources to A.
records.formal_summary: In SRC-0031's inspected convention, R is Schnorr random relative to A if for some A-recursive rate r there are no A-recursive martingale mg and A-recursive bound f for which mg on the f(n)-length prefix of R exceeds r(n) for infinitely many n.
cautions: This record preserves the source's martingale/rate wording rather than asserting an uninspected equivalence with every oracle-Schnorr test normalization.
Uniformly relative/truth-table Schnorr randomness DEF-0024 is a distinct weaker relativization in SRC-0032.

records.name: Kurtz randomness relative to an oracle A (martingale relativization in SRC-0031)
records.object_domain: oracle A and infinite binary sequence R
records.effective_resources: A-recursive rate function r, A-recursive martingale mg and A-recursive bound function f in Property 1.1
records.measure_assumptions: binary fair-betting/Cantor-space setting of the inspected paper
records.relativization: Property 1.1 relativizes the rate, martingale and bound resources to A.
records.formal_summary: In SRC-0031's inspected convention, R is Kurtz random relative to A if for some A-recursive rate r there are no A-recursive martingale mg and A-recursive bound f for which mg on the f(n)-length prefix of R exceeds r(n) for all n.
cautions: This is a source-specific ordinary oracle martingale formulation; P1-S003 does not infer equivalence with uninspected alternative oracle-Kurtz normal forms.

records.name: Uniformly relative Schnorr randomness
records.object_domain: A,B∈2^ω
records.effective_resources: a total computable map Φ:2^ω→N^N whose every oracle instance encodes a Schnorr test
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space
records.relativization: The oracle B selects an instance from a single total computable family rather than allowing arbitrary B-computable test code.
aliases: Schnorr random uniformly relative to B
records.formal_summary: A is Schnorr random uniformly relative to B iff no uniform Schnorr-test family has its B-instance cover A at every level.
cautions: SRC-0032 explicitly distinguishes this weaker uniform relativization from usual/ordinary relative Schnorr randomness DEF-0022.

records.name: Uniformly relative computable randomness
records.object_domain: A,B∈2^ω
records.effective_resources: a total computable map Φ:2^ω→N^N whose every oracle instance encodes a martingale
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin martingale setting on Cantor space
records.relativization: The oracle B selects a martingale from one total computable family.
aliases: computably random uniformly relative to B
records.formal_summary: A is computably random uniformly relative to B iff no uniform martingale family has a B-instance that succeeds on A.
cautions: This is weaker than ordinary computable randomness relative to B in the sense witnessed by SRC-0032 Corollary 5.4 (THM-0025).
SRC-0032's computable-randomness van-Lambalgen theorem is symmetric: each half is uniformly random relative to the other; do not rewrite it as the asymmetric ML theorem.

records.name: Demuth randomness
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real Z in Cantor space 2^ω in the modern inspected formulation; Demuth's 1982 original is formulated for arithmetical reals
records.effective_resources: c.e. open test components whose indices are given by an ω-c.e. function f (equivalently in SRC-0016, f≤wtt∅'), so the index for level m changes only a computably bounded number of times depending on m
records.framework: moving-component effective null test with computably bounded mind changes and Solovay passing
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space in the modern inspected sources; each final component has measure at most 2^-m
records.relativization: No oracle-relative variant is normalized in P1-S004. The record is ordinary fair-coin Demuth randomness.
aliases: NWAP (later historical Demuth terminology reported by SRC-0016)
A_beta (1982 historical class notation as decoded by SRC-0016)
records.formal_summary: A Demuth test has final c.e. open components U_m=[W_{f(m)}]^≺ with μ(U_m)≤2^-m, where f is ω-c.e. and the number of changes in an approximation to f(m) is computably bounded as a function of m. Z passes in the Solovay sense: Z belongs to only finitely many final U_m. Z is Demuth random iff it passes every Demuth test.
cautions: The 1982 original uses a restricted arithmetical-real domain and Demuth's own formal notation; the modern all-real Cantor-space wording is not attributed verbatim to SRC-0034.

Demuth passing is Solovay passing (membership in only finitely many final components), not merely escaping one component. Balanced and Oberwolfach randomness use the weak-Demuth/ordinary escape convention in the inspected sources.
Historical labels WAP/NWAP and A_alpha/A_beta are source-era terminology; do not use them as context-free modern synonyms.

records.name: Difference randomness
records.object_domain: real A in fair-coin Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: recursive index functions for c.e. sets of strings; a d.r.e. test component is a difference D(U,V)=[U]\[V], and the general n-r.e. component alternates finitely many such c.e.-open pieces as in SRC-0035
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure; each i-th test component has measure at most 2^-i
records.relativization: No oracle-relative difference-randomness definition is promoted in P1-S004; only the ordinary fair-coin definition is recorded.
aliases: 2-r.e. random in the neighborhood-based hierarchy of SRC-0035
records.formal_summary: A d.r.e. test is a uniformly effectively indexed sequence of sets D(W_{g1(i)},W_{g2(i)})=[W_{g1(i)}]\[W_{g2(i)}] with measure at most 2^-i. A real is difference random iff it escapes the intersection of every such test. SRC-0035 proves that the corresponding neighborhood-based n-r.e. randomness notions coincide for all n≥2.
cautions: SRC-0035 also defines a separate naive n-r.e. string-test notion and proves that for n≥2 it coincides with 2-randomness. That naive notion is not difference randomness.
The n-r.e. label is therefore source-sensitive: retain the neighborhood/difference semantics before translating the term.

records.name: Balanced randomness
records.object_domain: real Z in fair-coin Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: c.e. open components G_m=[W_{f(m)}]^≺ with a computable approximation f(m)=lim_s g(m,s); the number of changes of g(m,·) is O(2^m), equivalently an exact 2^m change bound in the source's normal form
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure; μ(G_m)≤2^-m
records.relativization: No oracle-relative balanced-randomness definition is normalized in P1-S004.
records.formal_summary: A balanced test is a weak-Demuth-style moving-component test (G_m) with μ(G_m)≤2^-m whose m-th index changes O(2^m) times. A real passes by escaping at least one final component; it is balanced random iff it passes every balanced test. SRC-0036 shows the O(2^m) bound can be normalized to exactly 2^m changes without changing the notion.
cautions: Balanced randomness is formulated as a restricted weak-Demuth notion: ordinary escape from a component is the passing condition. Do not replace it with Demuth's Solovay/finitely-many-components passing convention.

records.name: Oberwolfach randomness
records.object_domain: real / set Z in fair-coin Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: weak Demuth test components U_n with computably bounded version changes, plus a coherence constraint linking changes at adjacent levels
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure; μ(U_n)≤2^-n in the inspected source
records.relativization: No oracle-relative Oberwolfach-randomness definition is normalized in P1-S004.
records.formal_summary: An Oberwolfach test is a weak Demuth test with coherent component changes: for every n and every interval of stages on which the n-th component remains unchanged, the (n+1)-st component changes at most once. A real is Oberwolfach random iff it passes every such test in the ordinary weak-Demuth sense.
cautions: The coherence condition, not an O(2^n) numerical bound, is the defining extra constraint over weak Demuth tests.
P1-S004 records only the source's fair-coin Cantor-space form and does not transfer it to arbitrary computable measures or oracle relativizations.

records.name: Computable metric space (Hoyrup-Rojas randomness framework)
records.object_domain: complete separable metric space (X,d) with a numbered countable dense set S={s_i}
records.effective_resources: the real distances d(s_i,s_j) are uniformly computable; points are represented by fast Cauchy names of ideal points; basic opens are rational ideal balls
records.measure_assumptions: none at this definition level
records.relativization: not an oracle-randomness notion
records.formal_summary: A computable metric space is a complete separable metric space with a dense numbered set of ideal points whose pairwise distances are uniformly computable. The canonical point representation uses rapidly convergent Cauchy sequences of ideal points; ideal balls form the effective basis.
cautions: This is the specific computable-metric-space representation used by the inspected sources; P1-S005 does not promote a theorem for arbitrary represented spaces.

records.name: Computable probability measure on a computable metric space
records.object_domain: Borel probability measure μ on a computable metric space X
records.effective_resources: μ is a computable point of the computable metric space of Borel probability measures under the Prokhorov metric with finite rational discrete ideal measures; equivalently open-set valuation is lower semicomputable
records.measure_assumptions: probability measure; no atomlessness or full-support assumption in the definition
records.relativization: not applicable
records.formal_summary: μ is computable when it is a computable point of the represented metric space M(X) of Borel probability measures. Equivalently, μ(U) is lower semicomputable uniformly for open U, and it suffices uniformly for finite unions of ideal balls. On Cantor space this specializes to uniform computability of cylinder measures.
cautions: Atomlessness is not part of computability of a measure. It appears only in stronger isomorphism results such as THM-0034.
Non-full support is allowed; density claims for representation domains must be read relative to the support qualification in SRC-0011.

records.name: Computable probability space
records.object_domain: pair (X,μ) with X a computable metric space and μ a Borel probability measure on X
records.effective_resources: X carries the canonical computable-metric representation and μ is computable as DEF-0031
records.measure_assumptions: μ is computable; atoms and non-full support are allowed unless a theorem states otherwise
records.relativization: not an oracle-randomness notion
records.formal_summary: A computable probability space is a computable metric space X equipped with a computable Borel probability measure μ.
cautions: This record follows the inspected computable-metric-space literature; it is not a blanket synonym for every represented probability-space formalism.

records.name: Martin-Löf randomness on a computable probability space
records.object_domain: point x in a computable probability space (X,μ)
records.effective_resources: uniformly r.e./effectively open test components in the effective basis; equivalent lower-semicomputable integral-test formulation is available in SRC-0011
records.measure_assumptions: μ is computable; a test has μ(A_n)≤2^-n; no atomlessness or full-support assumption
records.relativization: measure-parameter uniformity is treated separately by DEF-0006
aliases: Martin-Löf random point in a computable probability space
records.formal_summary: A Martin-Löf test on (X,μ) is a uniformly effectively open sequence (A_n) with μ(A_n)≤2^-n. A point is μ-Martin-Löf random iff it belongs to no intersection of such a test. SRC-0011 gives the equivalent lower-semicomputable integral-test/random-point formulation.
cautions: DEF-0002 remains the fair-coin Cantor-space specialization; do not silently transfer fair-coin-only theorems to this record.

records.name: Schnorr randomness on a computable probability space
records.object_domain: point x in a computable probability space (X,μ)
records.effective_resources: a Martin-Löf test (A_n) whose real component measures μ(A_n) are uniformly computable in n
records.framework: effective null tests with computable level measures
records.measure_assumptions: μ is computable; A_n are uniformly effectively open, μ(A_n)≤2^-n, and n↦μ(A_n) is computable; no atomlessness/full-support assumption
records.relativization: ordinary/uniform oracle relativization from P1-S003 is a different axis and is not folded into this definition
records.formal_summary: A Schnorr test on a computable probability space is a Martin-Löf test whose component measures form a uniformly computable sequence of reals. A point is Schnorr random iff it fails no such test.
cautions: The exact-equality μ(A_n)=2^-n normal form used in some fair-coin sources is not inserted here; SRC-0012 states the computable-level-measure condition.
DEF-0003 remains the fair-coin Cantor-space record.

records.name: Morphism and isomorphism of computable probability spaces
records.object_domain: maps between computable probability spaces (X,μ) and (Y,ν)
records.effective_resources: a morphism is μ-computable/a.e.-computable on a constructive G_delta domain of μ-measure one and measure-preserving; an isomorphism uses morphisms in both directions with the inverse identities on the prescribed full-measure domains
records.measure_assumptions: source and target are computable probability spaces; no atomlessness is required for the general morphism/isomorphism definitions
records.relativization: not applicable
records.formal_summary: A morphism is an effectively given almost-everywhere map that pushes μ forward to ν. An isomorphism is a pair of such morphisms satisfying inverse identities on the corresponding full-measure domain sets.
cautions: A general isomorphism to Cantor space is with an appropriate computable measure, not necessarily fair coin; see THM-0033.
Atomlessness is required for the stronger computable-Lebesgue-space theorem THM-0034.

records.name: Computable randomness for a computable measure on Cantor space (Rute integral-test form)
records.object_domain: x∈2^ω with computable Borel measure μ on Cantor space
records.effective_resources: lower-semicomputable t together with a computable probability measure ν satisfying ∫_[σ] t dμ≤ν(σ) for every cylinder [σ]; equivalently the source gives the computable-measure martingale-ratio form
records.measure_assumptions: μ is a computable probability measure on Cantor space; the equivalent ratio formulation additionally requires μ(x↾n)>0 along the tested real
records.relativization: uniform relativization is outside this record; Rute separately labels a uniform-relativized extension as conjectural in the inspected paper
aliases: computable randomness with respect to μ
records.formal_summary: x is μ-computably random iff every Rute test pair (t,ν) satisfying the cylinderwise integral domination keeps t(x) finite. Equivalently, μ(x↾n)>0 for all n and for every computable measure ν the ratio ν(x↾n)/μ(x↾n) has finite liminf.
cautions: This is an arbitrary-computable-measure Cantor-space definition, not a claim that the fair-coin martingale equation in DEF-0004 transfers verbatim to every computable probability space.
The paper's proposed fully uniform-relativized NRFN extension is Conjecture 21, not promoted here as a theorem.

records.name: Effective meagreness on Cantor space
records.object_domain: subset F of Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: an effective F_sigma cover ⋃_m C_m with the C_m uniformly Π^0_1 and each C_m nowhere dense
records.measure_assumptions: none; smallness is topological/category-theoretic, not defined by probability measure
records.relativization: P1-S006 records only the unrelativized definition; oracle-effective variants occur in SRC-0043 but are not separately normalized here.
records.formal_summary: F⊆2^ω is effectively meagre if F is contained in an effective F_sigma class ⋃_m C_m where (C_m)_m is a uniform sequence of Π^0_1 classes and every C_m is nowhere dense. For such Π^0_1 components, from m and a finite string σ one can effectively find an extension ρ⊒σ whose cylinder misses C_m.
cautions: This is a category notion: no test-level probability bound or null-measure hypothesis is part of the definition.
SRC-0043 sometimes also works in Baire space; this record fixes the explicitly stated Cantor-space version rather than silently identifying the two presentations.

records.name: Weak 1-genericity
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real X in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: dense computably enumerable (Σ^0_1) sets of finite binary strings, equivalently dense effectively open classes
records.measure_assumptions: none in the definition; the Kurtz-random comparison is a separate primary-source theorem
records.relativization: P1-S006 does not reopen the oracle-genericity survey. SRC-0031/SRC-0041 contain relative variants, but this record is unrelativized.
aliases: weak genericity (when the level is explicitly 1)
records.formal_summary: X is weakly 1-generic iff X meets every dense c.e. set of finite binary strings (equivalently, X belongs to every dense Σ^0_1 open class). In the effective-category formulation of SRC-0043 this is equivalently avoidance of every effectively meagre set in the sense of DEF-0037.

source_support.pointer: Introduction, n=1 specialization of weak n-genericity

cautions: Do not identify weak 1-genericity with 1-genericity (DEF-0039).
Do not identify weakly 1-generic with weakly 1-random/Kurtz random (DEF-0013): REL-0037 is a strict implication, not an equivalence.
The word 'weak' here belongs to the genericity hierarchy and is unrelated to the weak-n-randomness indexing in DEF-0014.

records.name: 1-genericity on Cantor space
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence x in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: c.e. subsets A⊆2^{<ω}; x must meet each A that is dense along x
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: P1-S006 records the unrelativized Σ^0_1-generic notion only.
records.formal_summary: For A⊆2^{<ω}, x meets A if some prefix of x lies in A; A is dense along x if every prefix σ⊑x has an extension τ⊒σ with [τ]⊆[A]. Then x is 1-generic iff it meets every c.e. A that is dense along x. Equivalently, for every Π^0_1 class V, x avoids V\Int(V).
cautions: Dense-along-x is local to x and is not the same quantifier pattern as meeting every globally dense c.e. set; the latter is weak 1-genericity.
No probability measure appears in this definition.

records.name: Weak n-genericity
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real A in Cantor space 2^ω, with integer n≥1
records.effective_resources: dense Σ^0_n sets of finite binary strings
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: Not separately normalized in P1-S006; this parameter n is an arithmetical-complexity level, not the repository's weak-n-randomness notion.
records.formal_summary: For n≥1, A is weakly n-generic iff A meets every dense Σ^0_n set of finite binary strings.

source_support.pointer: publisher extract for original provenance only

cautions: Weak n-genericity is a category/genericity hierarchy and must not be confused with weak n-randomness (DEF-0014), which is measure-one typicality.
Unqualified 'weak genericity' is ambiguous unless the level is stated.

records.name: n-genericity
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence / real A in Cantor space 2^ω, with integer n≥1
records.effective_resources: Σ^0_n sets S of finite binary strings; finite-extension meet-or-avoid requirement
records.framework: arithmetical hierarchy of effective category / Cohen genericity
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: SRC-0044 notes the standard jump-relative reformulation, but P1-S006 does not open a new oracle-genericity record and leaves DEF-0020's n-random jump convention unchanged.
records.formal_summary: For n≥1, A is n-generic iff for every Σ^0_n set S⊆2^{<ω}, there is a prefix σ⊑A such that either σ∈S or no extension τ⊒σ lies in S.

source_support.pointer: foundational provenance only; internal statement not inspected

cautions: Do not collapse n-genericity with weak n-genericity; the source-stated hierarchies interleave.
The symbol n here indexes arithmetical genericity requirements, not a probability-test bound or the weak-n-randomness class.

records.name: Left-c.e. real
records.object_domain: real number α; the inspected Ω sources principally work in (0,1] or identify such reals with binary sequences
records.effective_resources: a computable/recursive nondecreasing sequence of rational numbers converging to α
records.measure_assumptions: none in the definition
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S007
aliases: recursively enumerable real (historical terminology in SRC-0046/SRC-0047)
records.formal_summary: A real α is left-c.e. iff there is a computable nondecreasing sequence of rationals (q_s) with lim_s q_s=α. SRC-0046 and SRC-0047 use the historical term 'recursively enumerable real' for this one-sided approximation notion.

source_support.pointer: §4, definition before Theorem 4.1 and Theorem 4.1(1)-(3), printed pp. 131-132

cautions: Left-c.e. is an approximation/computability property, not a randomness property. Arbitrary left-c.e. reals must not be identified with the random left-c.e. subclass.
The terminology normalization from 'r.e. real' to 'left-c.e. real' is recorded explicitly; no theorem is being changed by the vocabulary update.

records.name: Halting probability of a prefix-free machine
records.object_domain: prefix-free/self-delimiting partial computable machine M on finite binary strings and the associated real Ω_M∈[0,1]
records.effective_resources: c.e. prefix-free domain dom(M)
records.framework: fair-coin input measure / Kraft sum of halting programs
records.measure_assumptions: each finite program p has cylinder weight 2^{-|p|}; prefix-freeness makes the sum at most 1
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S007
aliases: measure of the domain of a prefix-free machine
records.formal_summary: For a prefix-free/self-delimiting partial computable machine M, Ω_M=Σ_{p∈dom(M)}2^{-|p|}. This definition does not require M to be universal.

source_support.pointer: Definition 1.4 and preceding self-delimiting convention, printed p. 200
§3 and Theorem 4.1 with footnote 6, printed pp. 129-132

cautions: Universality is not part of this definition. A halting probability of an arbitrary prefix-free machine need not be Martin-Löf random.
P1-S007 reserves 'Chaitin Ω-number' for DEF-0044, where universality is explicit.

records.name: Chaitin Ω-number
records.object_domain: real Ω_U associated with a universal self-delimiting/prefix-free machine U
records.effective_resources: a Chaitin-universal / universal self-delimiting partial computable machine
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin weight 2^{-|p|} on each halting program p
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S007; SRC-0030's separate relative-Ω topic is not reopened
records.formal_summary: A Chaitin Ω-number is Ω_U=Σ_{U(p)↓}2^{-|p|} for a universal self-delimiting/prefix-free machine U. Universality is substantive: it is what distinguishes Ω-numbers from arbitrary prefix-free halting probabilities.

source_support.pointer: Definition of the Probability ω that U Halts and Theorem 4.3 in the article reprint
§3, universal self-delimiting machine and Ω_U convention, printed pp. 129-130

cautions: The numerical value depends on the chosen universal machine U; 'Ω' is therefore a machine-relative notation unless U has been fixed.
Do not call the halting probability of a merely prefix-free, nonuniversal machine a Chaitin Ω-number in this catalogue.

records.name: Binary real / infinite-sequence representation convention
records.object_domain: real x∈(0,1] and an infinite binary expansion representing x
records.effective_resources: none
records.framework: representation convention connecting real numbers with Cantor-space sequences
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: not applicable
records.formal_summary: When a real is treated as an infinite binary sequence, the binary expansion convention must be fixed. SRC-0045 chooses, for x∈(0,1], the unique expansion with infinitely many 1s. SRC-0047 instead states the identification explicitly and notes uniqueness for irrational reals; Ω-numbers are random and hence irrational.

source_support.pointer: Definition of Base-Two Representations in the article reprint, printed p. 216
finite/infinite sequence notation and Convention 1.5, printed pp. 199-200
Ω binary-expansion convention and irrationality footnote, printed p. 130

cautions: Dyadic rationals have two ordinary binary expansions, so an arbitrary real cannot be silently identified with a unique binary sequence without a convention.
For Ω itself the ambiguity disappears because the inspected sources establish randomness and hence irrationality.

records.name: Computational indistinguishability of probability ensembles (bounded-adversary form)
records.object_domain: two probability ensembles D=(D_n) and E=(E_n), each D_n/E_n a distribution on finite binary strings of the prescribed length for security parameter n
records.effective_resources: bounded statistical distinguishers/adversaries; Yao's foundational form uses polynomial statistical tests, while SRC-0049 parameterizes adversary running time and distinguishing success/security
records.measure_assumptions: probabilities are over the sampled finite strings and any internal randomness of the test/adversary; no Cantor-space null-test semantics is assumed
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S008
records.formal_summary: Two indexed distributions on finite strings are computationally indistinguishable when the allowed resource-bounded observers cannot distinguish which ensemble supplied a sample with the prohibited level of advantage. P1-S008 retains the source-specific quantitative security convention rather than replacing it with an uninspected normal form.

source_support.pointer: printed p. 84, polynomial statistical tests and Theorem 3

cautions: This is a relation between probability ensembles/distributions on finite strings, not an intrinsic property of one infinite binary sequence.
Do not identify computational indistinguishability with Martin-Löf, Schnorr or computable randomness. Their objects and testing resources differ.
The source-specific bound on the distinguisher/adversary is part of the definition and must not be erased.

records.name: Pseudorandom generator (finite-seed distribution-ensemble form)
records.object_domain: a deterministic P-time function ensemble g mapping finite seeds of length t_n to finite outputs of length l_n with l_n>t_n
records.effective_resources: P-time generation plus the bounded distinguisher/adversary class used in DEF-0046
records.measure_assumptions: the seed is sampled uniformly; the induced output distribution g(U_{t_n}) is compared with the uniform distribution U_{l_n} on finite output strings
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S008
records.formal_summary: In SRC-0049, a P-time stretching function ensemble g is pseudorandom when the induced output ensemble on a uniformly random seed is computationally indistinguishable, at the stated security level, from the uniform output ensemble of the same length. SRC-0048 supplies the foundational polynomial-test source-ensemble viewpoint.

source_support.pointer: printed p. 84, source/test definitions and Theorem 3

cautions: The randomness claim is distributional over a uniformly sampled finite seed. It is not a claim that every fixed output string, or an infinite concatenation of outputs, is Martin-Löf/Schnorr/computably random.
Stretch and the computational resource bound are substantive parts of the notion.
No cryptographic security claim beyond the inspected source definitions is imported into the Fairfax-Ball catalogue.

records.name: Resource-bounded Δ-randomness of an infinite binary sequence (including p-randomness)
records.object_domain: individual infinite binary sequence x∈{0,1}^ω; complexity-theoretic languages are represented by their characteristic sequences under the source's fixed string ordering
records.effective_resources: a resource class Δ from SRC-0051's transduction classes; in particular p=p1 is the polynomial-time class, with p_i defined by G_i-time computation
records.measure_assumptions: a Δ-test is a subset X of Cantor space with resource-bounded measure μ_Δ(X)=1 in SRC-0051's measure theory; x passes X when x∈X
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S008
records.formal_summary: SRC-0051 defines x to be Δ-random when x belongs to every set of Δ-measure one. For Δ=p, where the paper writes p=p1 for polynomial-time transductions, this gives polynomial-time p-randomness of an individual infinite sequence.

source_support.pointer: resource classes on paper pp. 8-9; Definition 6.1 on paper p. 35

cautions: This is an individual-infinite-sequence notion, unlike DEF-0046/DEF-0047's finite-string probability ensembles.
The resource class Δ is part of the definition; dropping it changes the notion.
P1-S008 records no implication between p-randomness and the existing unbounded Martin-Löf/Schnorr/computable-randomness hierarchy.
The source's use of the word 'pseudorandom' here does not make this definition identical to a cryptographic PRG output ensemble.

records.name: Resource-bounded martingale success test (Lutz Δ-computable form)
records.object_domain: a martingale d on finite binary prefixes together with an individual infinite binary sequence x
records.effective_resources: d is Δ-computable for the chosen resource class Δ; p is the polynomial-time specialization from SRC-0051
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin martingale equality in SRC-0051's density-function/martingale framework
records.relativization: not treated in P1-S008
records.formal_summary: A martingale succeeds on x when its capital along the successive prefixes of x has unbounded limsup. Restricting the martingale to Δ-computable strategies supplies the betting characterization of Δ-randomness in THM-0050.

source_support.pointer: Definition 3.18, paper p. 20; Theorem 6.2, paper p. 35

cautions: The Δ-computability restriction is essential; this record must not be silently replaced by unrestricted or merely computable martingales.
This is the minimal P1-S008 bridge to the already catalogued martingale viewpoint; no hierarchy implication is inferred.

records.name: Δ1^1-randomness (hyperarithmetic randomness)
records.object_domain: individual real / infinite binary sequence X in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: lightface Δ1^1 (hyperarithmetic) definability of null sets of reals
records.framework: higher randomness by effective-descriptive-set-theoretic null-class avoidance
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space in the inspected sources
records.relativization: This is a higher-computability pointclass notion, not the finite jump-relativized n-randomness convention of DEF-0020.
records.formal_summary: X is Δ1^1-random iff X belongs to no null lightface Δ1^1 set of reals.
cautions: Do not obtain this notion by extending DEF-0020 to a transfinite n. The pointclass/effectivity resource is stated independently in the higher-randomness sources.
Δ1^1-Martin-Löf randomness is separately recorded as DEF-0051 and is equivalent only by the inspected theorem THM-0051.

records.name: Δ1^1-Martin-Löf randomness
records.object_domain: individual real / infinite binary sequence X in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: a Martin-Löf test (U_n) whose basic-cylinder code relation is lightface Δ1^1
records.framework: higher Martin-Löf tests at the Δ1^1 pointclass
records.measure_assumptions: each open test component U_n has μ(U_n) ≤ 2^-n under fair-coin/Lebesgue measure
records.relativization: Higher pointclass formulation; not an extension of the finite jump convention DEF-0020.
records.formal_summary: A Δ1^1-Martin-Löf test is an ω-sequence of open sets with μ(U_n)≤2^-n whose basic-cylinder coding relation is Δ1^1. X is Δ1^1-ML-random iff X is outside the intersection of every such test.
cautions: The equivalence with DEF-0050 is theorem-supported; it is not used as a definitional shortcut.

records.name: Π1^1-Martin-Löf randomness (higher Martin-Löf randomness)
records.object_domain: individual real / infinite binary sequence X in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: Π1^1-coded / higher-c.e. open test components; Hjorth-Nies equivalently use uniformly Σ1-definable-over-L_{ω1^CK} open sets
records.measure_assumptions: test components have μ(U_n) ≤ 2^-n under fair-coin/Lebesgue measure
records.relativization: Continuous higher relativization is separately defined through Π1^1 enumeration functionals in SRC-0054; ordinary oracle relativization must not be substituted automatically.
records.formal_summary: X is Π1^1-Martin-Löf random iff it passes every Martin-Löf test whose open components are uniformly available at the Π1^1/higher-c.e. level specified by the source.
cautions: Hjorth-Nies locally use the unqualified phrase 'ML-random' for this Π1^1 version; the catalogue qualifies it to avoid collision with ordinary Martin-Löf randomness DEF-0002.
Π1^1-Martin-Löf randomness is strictly weaker than Π1^1-randomness DEF-0053 by THM-0052.

records.name: Π1^1-randomness
records.object_domain: individual real / infinite binary sequence X in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: lightface Π1^1 definability of null sets of reals
records.framework: higher randomness by Π1^1 null-class avoidance
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin/Lebesgue measure on Cantor space
records.relativization: Not identified with finite jump-relativized n-randomness; P1-S009 records only the unrelativized higher notion.
aliases: Σ1^1-random (Sacks historical terminology, as reported by Hjorth-Nies)
records.formal_summary: X is Π1^1-random iff X avoids every null lightface Π1^1 set of reals; equivalently, X lies outside the largest null Π1^1 class whose existence is recorded in THM-0053.
cautions: Do not use 'Π1^1-randomness' and 'Π1^1-Martin-Löf randomness' as synonyms; the inspected sources separate them strictly.
Hjorth-Nies report the historical Sacks label 'Σ1^1-random' for this null-Π1^1-class notion. That historical name is preserved as provenance, not generalized as a pointclass-duality rule.

records.name: Higher weak 2-randomness
records.object_domain: individual real / infinite binary sequence X in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: uniformly Π1^1 (higher-c.e.) open sets forming a higher weak-2 test; equivalently the Π^ck_2 higher-arithmetic-hierarchy level in SRC-0055
records.framework: generalized higher Martin-Löf tests / higher arithmetic hierarchy
records.measure_assumptions: a higher weak 2-test has null intersection; the components may be taken nested
records.relativization: P1-S009 records the unrelativized higher notion only.
records.formal_summary: A higher weak 2-test is an ω-sequence of uniformly Π1^1 open (higher-c.e. open) sets whose intersection is null; it may be assumed nested. X is higher weak 2-random iff it avoids every such test.
cautions: This is not ordinary weak 2-randomness DEF-0015 and is not obtained by inserting a transfinite index into DEF-0020.
The hierarchy links recorded here are only the inspected higher-source links.

records.name: Higher difference randomness (continuous-higher formulation)
records.object_domain: a higher Martin-Löf-random individual real / infinite binary sequence X in Cantor space 2^ω
records.effective_resources: continuous higher computability: uniformly higher effectively open U_n, a higher effectively closed class P, or equivalently version-disjoint tests with a higher ω-computably approximable index function
records.framework: higher difference tests / continuous higher Turing reducibility
records.measure_assumptions: nested tests have μ(U_n ∩ P) ≤ 2^-n in the closed-class formulation
records.relativization: Uses SRC-0054's continuous higher-computability machinery; ordinary oracle relativization is not substituted.
records.formal_summary: For higher ML-random X, SRC-0054 characterizes higher difference randomness by avoidance of all nested tests U_n∩P with U_n uniformly higher effectively open, P higher effectively closed, and μ(U_n∩P)≤2^-n; equivalently Kleene's O is not continuously higher-Turing reducible to X.
cautions: This record follows the inspected higher primary formulation and does not transfer the lower difference-test definition DEF-0027 by analogy.
The characterization is stated for higher Martin-Löf-random X.

records.name: T-typical point in the Gács-Hoyrup-Rojas dynamical framework
records.object_domain: point x in a computable probability space (X,μ) equipped with a measure-preserving endomorphism T
records.effective_resources: the surrounding system/endomorphism is computable in the paper's computable-probability-space sense; typicality itself quantifies over bounded continuous observables
records.measure_assumptions: μ is the invariant computable probability measure; the definition itself does not assume atomlessness, while THM-0006 does
records.relativization: not an oracle-randomness notion
records.formal_summary: x is T-typical when for every bounded continuous f:X→R, the averages n^{-1}Σ_{i<n} f(T^i x) converge to ∫f dμ. The source remarks that its main theorem also shows the definition is unchanged if 'continuous' is replaced by 'computable'.

source_support.pointer: Definition 3.28 and Remark 3.29 / corresponding STACS numbering

cautions: This is equality-to-expectation typicality. It is stronger in wording than mere convergence ('weak Birkhoff') used in DEF-0059.
THM-0006's principal equivalence assumes the computable probability space has no atoms.

records.name: Polynomially mixing and independent systems in the Gács-Hoyrup-Rojas framework
records.object_domain: computable measure-preserving dynamical system (X,T,μ)
records.effective_resources: an essential countable family E={E_i} of almost-decidable events; computable correlation-decay constants c_{i,j} and a polynomial exponent α>0
records.measure_assumptions: μ is T-invariant; correlation C_n(A,B)=μ(T^{-n}A∩B)-μ(A)μ(B) on the designated event family
records.relativization: not applicable
records.formal_summary: The system is polynomially mixing if some α>0 and essential family of almost-decidable events E satisfy |C_n(E_i,E_j)|≤c_{i,j}/n^α for all n≥1, with c_{i,j}>0 computable from i,j. It is independent when these correlations are eventually 0.
cautions: 'Mixing' here is the paper's effective polynomial-correlation condition, not an unqualified import of every classical mixing notion.
THM-0006 separately requires the ambient computable probability space to be atomless.

records.name: μ-layerwise computable function
records.object_domain: function f:X→Y between computable metric spaces, with X carrying computable probability measure μ
records.effective_resources: a universal μ-Martin-Löf test induces increasing random layers R_n^μ; f is computable on each R_n^μ uniformly in n
records.measure_assumptions: (X,μ) is a computable probability space
records.relativization: the layer index comes from a universal μ-Martin-Löf test, not ordinary oracle relativization
records.formal_summary: Let R^μ=⋃_n R_n^μ be the canonical Martin-Löf-random layers from a universal μ-test. A function is μ-layerwise computable when its restriction to every R_n^μ is computable uniformly in n.

source_support.pointer: Section 3.3, definition following the universal-test layer decomposition

cautions: Composition is not automatically layerwise computable; SRC-0057 adds a measure-preservation condition for the composition principle used in the ergodic arguments.
Layerwise computability is not the same resource as ordinary oracle relativization or the measure-parameter uniform tests of DEF-0006.

records.name: Weak Birkhoff point and Birkhoff point relative to an observable class
records.object_domain: point x in a probability space X with measure-preserving transformation T and a designated class F⊂L1
records.effective_resources: resource depends on the chosen transformation/observable class in the theorem using the definition
records.measure_assumptions: T is measure-preserving; observables are integrable
records.relativization: not applicable
records.formal_summary: x is weak Birkhoff for (T,F) when the Birkhoff average converges for every f∈F. It is Birkhoff for (T,F) when, additionally, each limit equals ∫f dμ.
cautions: In nonergodic systems, convergence alone does not identify the limit with the space expectation.
The Franklin-Towsner characterization theorems recorded in P1-S010 are fair-coin Cantor-space results; this general definition does not by itself generalize them.

records.name: Martin-Löf 1966 randomness via a universal sequential test (fair-coin historical form)
records.object_domain: infinite binary sequence X in 2^ω, represented through its finite prefixes
records.effective_resources: an r.e. set U⊆N×2^{<ω} of critical regions; levels are nested with significance, extension-closed, and effectively enumerable
records.framework: historical sequential stochasticity tests / constructive null sets
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin measure; for each level m and string length n the level contains at most 2^{n-m} strings of length n, equivalently the induced open level has measure at most 2^-m
records.relativization: none in this historical record; ordinary oracle relativization remains DEF-0019
records.formal_summary: In SRC-0001 Section III, a sequential test is an r.e. family U of nested, extension-closed critical regions satisfying the fair-coin level bound. A universal sequential test exists. For an infinite binary sequence X, the critical level m_U(X) is the limit/supremum of the critical levels of its prefixes; X is random iff this value is finite for a fixed universal sequential test.
cautions: This record preserves the original 1966 syntax. The modern fair-coin uniformly effectively open formulation is DEF-0002.
The level parameter in the source starts at m=1 and the test is nested/extension-closed by definition; these are historical normal-form choices, not extra modern randomness strength.
Section IV of SRC-0001 treats arbitrary computable sequential distributions separately; no generalized computable-probability-space theorem is imported into this record.

records.name: Solovay test for Martin-Löf randomness (ordinary fair-coin form)
records.object_domain: computable sequence (σ_i) of finite binary strings, identified with basic cylinders in fair-coin Cantor space
records.effective_resources: the string sequence is computable; the Kraft sum Σ_i 2^{-|σ_i|} is finite/bounded, with no requirement that its value be computable
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin measure on Cantor space
records.relativization: not treated in the inspected source record
records.formal_summary: A Solovay test is a computable sequence of finite strings (σ_i) with bounded Σ_i2^{-|σ_i|}. A real passes/avoids the test iff only finitely many σ_i are prefixes of it.
cautions: Do not conflate this with DEF-0017, the Schnorr total-Solovay form, which additionally requires the finite total measure sum to be a computable real.
The inspected later primary source attributes this characterization to Solovay [Sol75], but that original draft remains uninspected in the catalogue.

records.name: c.e. martingale used in the Martin-Löf-randomness characterization
records.object_domain: nonnegative real-valued function f on finite binary strings
records.effective_resources: f(σ) is uniformly computably approximable from below by a nondecreasing computable rational sequence
records.measure_assumptions: fair-coin martingale equality f(σ0)+f(σ1)=2f(σ)
records.relativization: not treated in the inspected source record
records.formal_summary: A c.e. martingale is f:2^{<ω}→R_{≥0} satisfying f(σ0)+f(σ1)=2f(σ), with all values uniformly approximable from below. It succeeds on X in SRC-0059 when lim_n f(X↾n)=∞.
cautions: The resource is lower semicomputability/c.e., not computability. Do not replace it by the computable-martingale resource used for computable randomness.
The success convention in the inspected source is actual divergence of capital to +∞, not merely an unqualified limsup statement.
No arbitrary-measure or supermartingale generalization is asserted in this record.

records.name: Low for prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity K
records.object_domain: oracle/set A
records.effective_resources: prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity K and oracle prefix-free complexity K^A on finite strings
records.measure_assumptions: none
records.relativization: A is used as an oracle by the prefix-free machines defining K^A; this is complexity relativization, not itself a randomness-test definition.
records.formal_summary: A is low for K iff there is a constant c such that for every finite binary string σ, K^A(σ) ≥ K(σ)-c (equivalently K(σ) ≤ K^A(σ)+O(1)).
cautions: This is a finite-string oracle-complexity notion. It must not be rewritten as an infinite-sequence randomness predicate.
Low for K, K-triviality and low for Martin-Löf randomness are kept as separate definitions and connected only by THM-0069/THM-0070/THM-0003.
The direction K^A(σ)≤K(σ)+O(1) is automatic because an oracle machine can ignore its oracle; lowness requires the reverse inequality up to a constant.

records.name: Endomorphism randomness
records.object_domain: point x in a computable probability space (X,mu)
records.effective_resources: all a.e.-computable measure-preserving endomorphisms T:(X,mu)->(X,mu)
records.framework: preservation of computable randomness under all endomorphisms
records.measure_assumptions: general computable probability space; the Cantor fair-coin specialization is atomless
records.relativization: not applicable
records.formal_summary: x is endomorphism random iff T(x) is computably random for every a.e.-computable measure-preserving endomorphism T of the ambient computable probability space.
cautions: The source endomorphism class is a.e.-computable, not everywhere-total.
No finite-to-one or uniformly bounded fibre hypothesis is part of the definition.
Do not identify this notion with CAND-01's restricted R_fin predicate.
